pages.text:
Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431199




Summary of practice

1. Listen and follow the guided dreaming practice for audios 1 and 2. You may
want to listen more than once.

2. Contemplate the life of your parents, or whoever raised you from their
viewpoint. The guided dreaming exercise should start a process of seeing your parents
differently. Seeing their challenges, limitations, sacrifices, and hard choices they had to
make.

3. Write about the life of your parents from their viewpoint. This can be
beneficial if you have difficulty visualizing or dreaming the exercise from the audio.
Different people’s minds will venture into different viewpoints in different ways.

4. Expand this exercise by imagining other people’s experience and choices from their
viewpoint. Maybe your boss, an employee, spouse, or partner.



Some notes

With the parents exercise you may have the experience of completely re-writing a lot of
your beliefs about what happened in your childhood. The same event from their point of
view may lead you to a completely different interpretation. What you believed growing up
may not be valid. This is a good thing.

Sometimes people do this, and they already knew their parents really well, and so there is
no surprises. That happens.

Others realize that they don’t know much and so they go and ask a lot of questions of their
parents. If their parents are not around, then they ask aunts and uncles.

Once you are able to see the viewpoint of your parents, you can continue the practice with
other people. Imagine what it is to be them. Include their whole background, history,
influence and limitations of parents, lack of parents, and how humans are shaped by their
circumstances. Economic, educational, and religious limitations. You have permission to
completely make it up.

You are building conscious awareness with compassion and understanding for others.





                                                                                                               1/2

If you have difficulty with a customer service person, can you slip into their world and life
for a minute? How about the challenges they face that you know nothing about. Perhaps
taking care of another customer is not the most important thing they have to do that day.
Maybe a family illness, their child struggling at school getting bullied, paying rent, is also
going on in their mind.

Maybe they are not thrilled to be solving your problem, because that is not their dream
job. But they need to work to provide for themselves, and pay off their student loans. They
got their education so they could have the life of their dreams that they were told to
believe in. Now, not only are they not in their dream life, they are in this service job trying
to pay off the debt they are in.

“Everyone is fighting a battle that you can not see.”

Perhaps you can get there by reading fiction, and understanding other people that way. Or
writing fiction. My friend’s daughter had an assignment in high school. She was to write
about someone else’s life. She wrote about a tollbooth attendant. She wrote about what it
was like on the highway smelling the fumes of vehicle exhaust. She wrote about it in detail
to the point that you could be there experiencing it.

That’s easier, we have all likely experienced the same external traffic going by us. It’s
another step to experience the inner world of someone else. It may take several efforts to
move your imagination that far.

Continue this practice with other people’s lives in small ways, or in large ways, to help
your conscious expansion. You will find that people have very strong beliefs, that they
may not have chosen, explaining why they do what they do.

Your greater understanding of people will go a long ways in dis-crediting the Judge.





                                                                                                               2/2

pages.text:
Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431200

I talked to a client who had done the Self Mastery II course about a year before. We got to
talking about this assignment and she confessed that she never did it. She was resisting it
for a year. That’s okay. If you find this one emotionally too much, maybe there was
trauma and violence in your childhood. Then put it aside. Maybe put it on your calendar
to consider doing in 6 or 12 months from now after you clear up much of that emotion.

I had another client. Her mother was schizophrenic. She never did the assignment either.
However in her own process, she could see her characters survival strategies with fears,
judgment, and anger. She could imagine not having any guidance about getting out of
them. A generation or two ago there wasn’t the mental health or medications support
there is today. She could easily see that her mother could be consumed by her characters.
She only had to see her own mind on a bad day and she could have understanding and
compassion for her mother.

When you really see the world through someone else’s viewpoint, you realize how artificial
and arbitrary all your stories and beliefs are. It shakes your sense of reality. Reality being
the way you have ordered explanations to fit together into a fabric of inter-connected
thoughts reinforcing each other, assuming other people are creating the same pattern.
You realize that others aren’t even building with the same materials much less design
pattern. Your’s is in wool, and their’s is in wood.

That kind of a shock to the belief system, like any big shift, can feel like someone just blew
up your map of the world and replaced it with a different one. North isn’t north, and west
isn’t west. It creates an unsettling feeling. Our tendency is to turn away from things that
create unsettling feeling. This is equal to dismissing the truth and clinging to an illusion.
Much in the way we have been NOT dealing with climate change. It is uncomfortable.
“Just give me my old map. I know my way around that one.”

Change involves moving through dissonance and uncomfortable feelings. That’s how
change happens. Do your best to embrace it. Revisit the releasing emotions exercise. As
beliefs change, emotions get released, and this comes in handy.





                                                                                                               1/1

title: Module 20-Viewpoint-20- SM - Viewpoint - 03 Common Questions
method: Text extracted from the original written course handout.

pages.text:
Common Questions

   selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-common-questions-6431201

What if you were adopted and not raised by your parents?

Do the process on whoever raised you, so that you can better understand their mindset,
behavior, choices, and emotions. Then you will better understand how and why they
treated you the way they did.

If it goes well, you can see that much of how they treated you wasn’t about you. It was all
about their conditioning that they didn’t choose.



Can you do this for your grandparents also?

Yes, please. Continue practicing other viewpoint from many different people. You may
find that, if they are still alive, that you will want to ask them about their life to help guide
you.

You may also find that this leads to deeper conversations with people as you ask them
more meaningful questions about their life.

I also suggest doing it with anyone you have conflicts with.



For extra credit

Dream the life of your spouse, ex partner, business partner, and especially people you
have conflicts with.





                                                                                                               1/1
